# Syntropy Earth

> Climate-health advisory. Climate change is a healthcare story: this site covers how a warming climate disrupts healthcare access, operations, supply chains and workforces, and what pharmaceutical, CSR, NGO and development finance teams can do about it. Based in Bengaluru, India, working globally.

Syntropy Earth is a climate-health strategy and advisory practice founded by Abhijith Magal L, who spent nine years across two global pharmaceutical multinationals before founding it, including brand and commercial work across more than 40 countries, a landmark obesity treatment launch, and health-equity and social responsibility leadership working directly with the WHO-Foundation and UNICEF.

The governing idea is that climate change reaches people first as a health and access problem rather than an environmental one, and that the organisations already carrying an obligation to respond are the ones who can move now. Work attaches to a budget that is already moving: mandated CSR spend under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, headquarters duty-of-care mandates, employer duty of care to a workforce, or a BRSR assurance clock.

## What Syntropy Earth does

- **Social responsibility programme design.** The flagship. Design a social responsibility programme around the company's own mission, built to survive a board question, an auditor, and a change of CSR head. Starts by reading the existing portfolio, because valuable work is usually already being undercounted or tagged against the wrong goal. Measurement mapped to BRSR and GRI. Optional scope modules for supply and cold chain resilience, facility resilience, workforce heat-health protocols, and community access mapping.
- **Health equity programme design.** For pharmaceutical, healthcare and diagnostics organisations. Patient access and health equity programmes with climate vulnerability inside the allocation logic from the first version. District-level access-barrier and disease-burden mapping, patient pathway design with seasonal disruption modelled, cold chain and last-mile continuity, governance separated from promotional activity.
- **Climate Access Stress Test (CAST).** The scored diagnostic. Four dimensions, four seasons, one score. Geographic exposure, supply chain and operational continuity, workforce availability, and financial and demand continuity, each read across heat, monsoon, air and drought. Includes pathway analysis of how one break cascades into others. Produces disclosure-ready climate-access metrics.
- **Implementation and handover.** Turns a design into a running programme, ending with a trained owner on the client side and a written operating manual. Partner screening, onboarding kit, governance model, monitoring system, disbursement and compliance calendar.
- **Advisory retainer.** Standing oversight of a live programme. Monthly strategic brief, running decision log, exposure watchlist, implementing-partner review, quarterly review pack. A separate lighter route exists for climate-health founders, requiring an existing product rather than an idea.
- **Climate literacy and speaking.** Leadership briefings and four-session working series built on a client's own exposure, plus university teaching and industry keynotes.
- **Launch readiness advisory.** Reads a launch plan against the four climate-access dimensions before access assumptions are locked in. Distribution reach in monsoon months, field force availability through peak heat, cold chain integrity, demand seasonality that moves with weather rather than the financial calendar.
- **Institutional programme work.** Programme structuring, research support, evidence synthesis and delivery model design for UN bodies, development finance institutions and foundations.

Explicitly not offered, and referred out: technical ESG, net-zero roadmapping, emissions accounting, disclosure assurance, and general brand or go-to-market consulting.

- [Thinking index](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/): Evidence-led writing on where climate change meets healthcare.
- [Climate Change Is a Healthcare Story](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-change-is-a-healthcare-story/): The core argument for reading climate as a health and access problem first.
- [Why the Heat Season Is a Healthcare Operations Problem](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/india-heat-season-healthcare-operations/): Extreme heat as a workforce, access and supply-chain problem, not just a medical one.
- [The Climate Risk Hiding in Your Access Data](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-risk-hiding-in-your-access-data/): How seasonal signals of climate disruption already sit in programme data nobody has read that way.
